Maya (support): customer reported tool-calling started failing after we rolled model v1-2 to canary this morning. payloads that worked on v1-1 are now returning schema errors.
Raj (eng-runtime): ugh. any error text from the API?
Maya (support): yes — upstream error from the inference service: `ToolCallValidationError: missing required property \"args.payload\"` even though customer is sending payload.
Emma (eng-ml): do we have an example request from them?
Maya (support): pasted below (sanitized):
```\nPOST /v1/chat/completions\n{\n  \"model\": \"redwood-model-1-2-canary\",\n  \"messages\": [{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"process this\"}],\n  \"functions\": [{\"name\":\"process\",\"parameters\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"payload\":{\"type\":\"object\"}},\"required\":[\"payload\"]}}],\n  \"function_call\": {\"name\":\"process\"},\n  \"args\": {\"payload\": {\"id\": 42, \"data\":\"x\"}}\n}\n```
Maya (support): but response shows validation failure as if args were empty.
Zoe (prod-ops): canary-bot: any anomalies in manifest or transform layers during the rollout?
canary-bot: alert: 1.2 canary traffic 12% -> observed tool-call validation error rate spike +0.9% over baseline @ 08:12 UTC.
Raj (eng-runtime): hmm maybe the new model's tool-calling schema extraction changed shape — could be the model returning `tool_call.arguments` as a stringified JSON instead of proper object, and our runtime then tries to map into args and fails validation.
Emma (eng-ml): that matches a known change: some model variants started returning `arguments` as compacted string to avoid tokenization problems. We usually parse if string, but maybe v1-2 introduced a nuance (escaped quotes) that breaks the parser.
Maya (support): the customer shared a full server response (trimmed):
```\n{\"id\":\"resp_123\",\"tool_call\":{\"name\":\"process\",\"arguments\":\"{\\\"payload\\\":{\\\"id\\\":42,\\\"data\\\":\\\"x\\\"}}\"}}\n```
Maya (support): they said this exact response worked with v1-1 cluster (we must have handled string-arguments before).
Raj (eng-runtime): can you repro locally by swapping model param to redwood-model-1-2-canary? I'll try parsing branch.
Zoe (prod-ops): deploy-bot: can you show rollout diff and which kernel/profile got toggled in canary?
deploy-bot: rollout 2026-03-17T07:50Z -> model redwood-model-1-2, changed tokenization-handling flag `normalize_tool_args=false` for canary nodes.
Raj (eng-runtime): there — that flag likely prevented the runtime from auto-parsing string-encoded arguments. On v1-1 it was true.
Emma (eng-ml): quick options: (A) runtime: add tolerant parse of stringified arguments (handle escaped quotes), (B) rollback the flag in canary to previous behavior, (C) ask model team to emit object not string.
Maya (support): customer is blocked in production, they ask for ETA or rollback.
Zoe (prod-ops): can we hotfix runtime parser quickly? how risky?
Raj (eng-runtime): low-risk change: if tool_call.arguments is string -> try JSON.parse with fallback to naive unescape. I can draft PR, but it needs canary deploy and smoke tests. Could be ~2-3 hours to ship and validate.
Emma (eng-ml): alternative: flip `normalize_tool_args` back to true for canary nodes — immediate rollback of change for canary only. That's a config flip and should be <15 minutes, but loses the model team's intended tweak.
Raj (eng-runtime): agree. for incident triage, flip the config for canary to restore compatibility, then follow up with a runtime parser hardening and a model-team sync.
Zoe (prod-ops): I can flip canary flag now if we decide. @Raj please prepare a rollback/flip playbook and monitoring check.
Maya (support): Customer wants a short mitigation message. Suggested: "We identified a compatibility regression in our canary model rollout that affects tool-call argument handling. We're reverting the canary configuration for now and will follow up once a fix is in place." ok?
Raj (eng-runtime): fine. also need to add repro steps to postmortem: curl example that reproduces the broken path.
Maya (support): adding repro to thread:
```\ncurl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat/completions \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-model-1-2-canary","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"x"}],"functions":[{"name":"process","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"payload":{"type":"object"}},"required":["payload"]}}],"function_call":{"name":"process"}}'\n```
Then inspect `tool_call.arguments` in the response.
Zoe (prod-ops): flipping flag now on canary path. I'll monitor error rate.
canary-bot: change applied: `normalize_tool_args=true` on canary nodes at 08:35 UTC.
canary-bot: error spike reduced to baseline within 6 minutes.
Maya (support): customer confirmed their calls succeed now. :white_check_mark:
Emma (eng-ml): next steps: follow-up items in backlog: 1) runtime tolerant parse, 2) add a unit test for string-arguments with escaped quotes, 3) model-team runbook to avoid changing argument serialization without a compat header.
Raj (eng-runtime): I'll open PR for parser and link this thread; will also add a canary alert that triggers on tool_call.arguments type drift.
Zoe (prod-ops): I'll log the rollback in release notes and tag the canary change for revert.
Maya (support): closing loop with customer, they'll watch for regression. thanks all. :heart:
